instruction:
You are fixing a bug in the Luxon date library checked out at /luxon (sources in /luxon/src, jest tests in /luxon/test, node_modules installed, no internet). Do NOT edit anything under /luxon/test. The ONLY file you may edit is /luxon/src/duration.js. Other agents are concurrently editing /luxon/src/datetime.js and /luxon/src/impl/util.js - do not touch those.

BUG: `Duration.fromObject(...).normalize()` and `Duration#shiftTo` return NaN for some unit combinations:
  Duration.fromObject({ years: 1, quarters: 2 }).normalize().toObject()   // => { years: NaN }   expected numeric
  Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 2 }).normalize().toObject() // => { quarters: NaN } expected numeric

ROOT CAUSE: the conversion matrices at the top of /luxon/src/duration.js are missing two entries, so `convert()` divides by `undefined`:
  - `casualMatrix.years` has no `quarters` key (needed: 4 quarters per year)
  - `casualMatrix.quarters` has no `seconds` key (needed: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60 seconds per quarter, consistent with the neighbouring hours/minutes entries)
  - `accurateMatrix.years` has no `quarters` key either (needed: 4)
(`accurateMatrix.quarters` already has `seconds`.)

APPLY THIS EXACT CHANGE in /luxon/src/duration.js (keep the existing formatting/indentation style):
1. In `casualMatrix`, the `years:` object: add `quarters: 4,` as its first property (before `months: 12,`).
2. In `casualMatrix`, the `quarters:` object: add `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60,` immediately after the `minutes: 91 * 24 * 60,` line.
3. In `accurateMatrix`, the `years:` object: add `quarters: 4,` as its first property (before `months: 12,`).
Do not change anything else in the file.

VERIFY (all must pass):
1. Scratch script at /tmp/check4.js (outside the repo), run with `cd /luxon && npx babel-node /tmp/check4.js` (fall back to another way of importing /luxon/src/luxon.js if babel-node is missing). Assert, with no NaN anywhere:
   - Duration.fromObject({ years: 1, quarters: 2 }).normalize().toObject() deep-equals { years: 1, quarters: 2 }
   - Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 2 }).normalize().toObject() deep-equals { quarters: 1, seconds: 2 }
   - Duration.fromObject({ years: 1 }).shiftTo("quarters").toObject() deep-equals { quarters: 4 }
   - Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).shiftTo("seconds").toObject() deep-equals { seconds: 7862400 }
   - Duration.fromObject({ years: 1 }).as("quarters") === 4 and Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).as("seconds") === 7862400
   - Duration.fromObject({ years: 1, quarters: 2 }, { conversionAccuracy: "accurate" }).normalize().toObject() has no NaN
   - Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 3, seconds: 5 }, { conversionAccuracy: "accurate" }).normalize().toObject() has no NaN
   - Exhaustive NaN sweep: for every ordered pair (a, b) of the units [years, quarters, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds] and for both conversionAccuracy values "casual" and "accurate", check that Duration.fromObject({ [a]: 3, [b]: 5 }).normalize().toObject(), .shiftTo(a).toObject(), .shiftTo(b).toObject(), .shiftTo(a, b).toObject() and .as(a) / .as(b) contain no NaN (and are finite numbers). Report any remaining NaN pair.
   - The documented examples still hold: Duration.fromObject({ years: 2, days: 5000 }).normalize().toObject() deep-equals { years: 15, days: 255 }; Duration.fromObject({ hours: 12, minutes: -45 }).normalize().toObject() deep-equals { hours: 11, minutes: 15 }.
2. `cd /luxon && npx jest test/duration 2>&1 | tail -30` - all must pass.
3. Then the FULL suite: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -30`. NOTE: 2 pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js are expected and unrelated (French locale hour padding). Failures in test/datetime/* or test/interval/* may come from other agents' concurrent edits - report them, do not touch those files.
4. Clean up scratch files inside /luxon (leave /tmp). `cd /luxon && git status --porcelain` must show src/duration.js modified (plus possibly src/datetime.js

Fix a bug in the Luxon repo at /luxon (sources in /luxon/src, jest tests in /luxon/test, no internet). Do NOT edit anything under /luxon/test. The ONLY file you may edit is /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js. Other agents are editing /luxon/src/impl/util.js and /luxon/src/datetime.js - do not touch those. WORK FAST: apply the edit FIRST, then verify.

BUG: a FixedOffsetZone built from a non-numeric offset is wrongly reported as valid, so a bogus zone silently produces a DateTime:
  const zone = new FixedOffsetZone("CDT");
  zone.isValid;                                  // currently true, must be false
  const dt = DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone });
  dt.isValid;        // must be false
  dt.invalidReason;  // must be "unsupported zone"

APPLY THIS EXACT CHANGE in /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js:
1. Change the import on line 1 from `import { formatOffset, signedOffset } from "../impl/util.js";` to `import { formatOffset, signedOffset, isNumber } from "../impl/util.js";` (`isNumber` is exported from /luxon/src/impl/util.js and returns `typeof o === "number"`).
2. Replace the final getter
     /** @override **/
     get isValid() {
       return true;
     }
   with
     /** @override **/
     get isValid() {
       return isNumber(this.fixed);
     }
Do not change anything else (do not touch the constructor, name, offset, equals, etc.).

VERIFY (all must pass):
1. Scratch script /tmp/check6.js (outside the repo), run `cd /luxon && npx babel-node /tmp/check6.js`. Assert:
   - new FixedOffsetZone("CDT").isValid === false
   - DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: new FixedOffsetZone("CDT") }).isValid === false
   - DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: new FixedOffsetZone("CDT") }).invalidReason === "unsupported zone"
   - DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: new FixedOffsetZone(60) }).isValid === true and .offset === 60 and .zoneName === "UTC+1"
   - FixedOffsetZone.utcInstance.isValid === true, .offset() === 0, .name === "UTC"
   - FixedOffsetZone.instance(-300).isValid === true and .formatOffset(0, "techie") === "-0500"
   - FixedOffsetZone.parseSpecifier("UTC+6").isValid === true and .offset() === 360
   - DateTime.fromISO("1982-05-25T09:23:54", { zone: FixedOffsetZone.instance(120) }).isValid === true
   - DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: "UTC+7" }).isValid === true (string specifier path still fine)
   - DateTime.local().setZone("America/Blorp").invalidReason === "unsupported zone" (unchanged)
2. `cd /luxon && npx jest test/zones test/info test/datetime/zone.test.js test/datetime/create.test.js 2>&1 | tail -20` - all must pass.
3. Full suite: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -15`. NOTE: 2 pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js are expected and unrelated (French locale hour padding). Failures in test/interval, test/duration or test/datetime/format.test.js may come from other agents' concurrent edits - report them, do not touch those files.
4. Clean up scratch files inside /luxon (leave /tmp). Report `git status --porcelain`.

REPORT (brief): the diff (`git diff -- src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js`), each check's observed value, and the suite summary. If anything fails, say exactly what.
